weekSubtitle: Blends, Power Words, Nouns & Subject-Verb Match

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Blends with L, R, S
lessons.description: Learn L, R, and S consonant blends, practice spelling words, and play Sort it!
lessons.hint: Say each blend sound quickly together like a train: s-p-ace → space!

cards.explanation: A blend is two or three letters that sit together. You say each sound quickly, like a train: s-p-ace → space!
cards.example: sp + ace → space 🚀
cards.speechText: Blends with L, R, S. A blend is two or three letters that sit together. You say each sound quickly, like a train: s-p-ace, space!

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (g + l → gl).
cards.example: We found Egypt on the classroom globe.
cards.speechText: Globe. G-L, globe. We found Egypt on the classroom globe.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (p + l → pl).
cards.example: This park is a fun place to play.
cards.speechText: Place. P-L, place. This park is a fun place to play.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (g + l → gl).
cards.example: Birds glide smoothly through the sky.
cards.speechText: Glide. G-L, glide. Birds glide smoothly through the sky.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (c + l → cl).
cards.example: Use a clip to hold your papers together.
cards.speechText: Clip. C-L, clip. Use a clip to hold your papers together.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (p + l → pl).
cards.example: Plug the lamp cord into the wall.
cards.speechText: Plug. P-L, plug. Plug the lamp cord into the wall.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (f + l → fl).
cards.example: Our flag waves high in the breeze.
cards.speechText: Flag. F-L, flag. Our flag waves high in the breeze.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (f + l → fl).
cards.example: The birthday candle has a warm flame.
cards.speechText: Flame. F-L, flame. The birthday candle has a warm flame.

cards.explanation: The second letter is L (s + l → sl).
cards.example: I ate a cheesy slice of pizza.
cards.speechText: Slice. S-L, slice. I ate a cheesy slice of pizza.

cards.explanation: A school mark. The second letter is R (g + r → gr).
cards.example: I got a great grade on my spelling work!
cards.speechText: Grade. A school mark. G-R, grade. I got a great grade on my spelling work!

cards.explanation: Pull something along. The second letter is R (d + r → dr).
cards.example: Do not drag your backpack on the floor.
cards.speechText: Drag. Pull something along. D-R, drag. Do not drag your backpack on the floor.

cards.explanation: The second letter is R (g + r → gr).
cards.example: Soft green grass grows in the yard.
cards.speechText: Grass. G-R, grass. Soft green grass grows in the yard.

cards.explanation: thr = 3 letters in a blend! t + h + r sit together.
cards.example: The king sat on a shiny gold throne.
cards.speechText: Throne. T-H-R is a 3 letter blend! The king sat on a shiny gold throne.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + p (sp).
cards.example: Astronauts travel far into space.
cards.speechText: Space. S-P, space. Astronauts travel far into space.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + w (sw).
cards.example: I can swim in the pool.
cards.speechText: Swim. S-W, swim. I can swim in the pool.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + k (sk).
cards.example: Sunscreen keeps your skin safe outside.
cards.speechText: Skin. S-K, skin. Sunscreen keeps your skin safe outside.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + n (sn).
cards.example: A long green snake slid through the grass.
cards.speechText: Snake. S-N, snake. A long green snake slid through the grass.

cards.explanation: Starts with S + t (st).
cards.example: Mom cooks warm soup on the stove.
cards.speechText: Stove. S-T, stove. Mom cooks warm soup on the stove.

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: I studied hard for my spelling test.
cards.speechText: Test. Ends with S-T. I studied hard for my spelling test.

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: This is the last lap of the race!
cards.speechText: Last. Ends with S-T. This is the last lap of the race!

cards.explanation: Ends with the -st blend (s + t).
cards.example: We just finished our homework!
cards.speechText: Just. Ends with S-T. We just finished our homework!

cards.explanation: Read each word out loud and spot the L, R, or S blend!
cards.speechText: Spelling words: space, globe, grade, swim, place, last, test, skin, drag, glide, just, stove. Extra review words: slid, close, grape, plate.

activity.title: Sort it!
activity.instruction: Tap or drag each word into the right blend box!

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Power Words
lessons.description: Learn all 8 Power Words with meanings, examples, tips, and play Match it!
lessons.hint: Read the meaning and the example sentence to picture the word!

cards.explanation: excellent, very good, or an expert.
cards.example: She is an ace at tennis.
cards.tip: Think of a top player or an A+ star!
cards.speechText: Ace. Excellent, very good, or an expert. She is an ace at tennis.

cards.explanation: with lots of excitement.
cards.example: He waited eagerly for the game.
cards.tip: When you can't wait for fun, you wait eagerly!
cards.speechText: Eagerly. With lots of excitement. He waited eagerly for the game.

cards.explanation: a group or company that gives a service to people.
cards.example: We asked a travel agency to plan our trip.
cards.tip: Helpers in an office who help plan things.
cards.speechText: Agency. A group or company that gives a service to people. We asked a travel agency to plan our trip.

cards.explanation: work of making, buying or selling things.
cards.example: Her family has a business.
cards.speechText: Business. Work of making, buying or selling things. Her family has a business.

cards.explanation: feeling sure of yourself.
cards.example: He answered confidently.
cards.tip: Stand tall because you know you are ready!
cards.speechText: Confidently. Feeling sure of yourself. He answered confidently.

cards.explanation: placed in a certain spot.
cards.example: The school is located near the park.
cards.tip: Located tells you WHERE something is.
cards.speechText: Located. Placed in a certain spot. The school is located near the park.

cards.explanation: something hard to understand or explain.
cards.example: The story was a mystery.
cards.tip: A puzzle that needs clues to solve!
cards.speechText: Mystery. Something hard to understand or explain. The story was a mystery.

cards.explanation: flows slowly through tiny holes.
cards.example: Water seeps from the wall.
cards.tip: Not a big splash—just slow drops coming through.
cards.speechText: Seeps. Flows slowly through tiny holes. Water seeps from the wall.

activity.title: Match it!
activity.instruction: Match 4 Power Words to their meanings!
allPairs: excellent, very good, or an expert
a company that gives a service
work of making, buying or selling things

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Singular & Plural Nouns
lessons.description: Learn ONE vs MORE THAN ONE nouns, when to add -s or -es, and play Add -s or -es?
lessons.hint: Look at the end of the word: s, x, ch, sh → add -es!

cards.explanation: A noun names a person, place, animal or thing.
cards.example: teacher 👩‍🏫 • park 🏞️ • cat 🐱 • book 📘
cards.speechText: What is a noun? A noun names a person, place, animal or thing. Like teacher, park, cat, or book.

cards.explanation: Singular = ONE (cat 🐱). Plural = MORE THAN ONE (cats 🐱🐱).
cards.example: 1 cat 🐱  →  3 cats 🐱🐱🐱
cards.speechText: Singular means one, like one cat. Plural means more than one, like three cats.

cards.explanation: Just put -s at the end to make most nouns plural!
cards.speechText: Rule 1: For most nouns, add s. Cat, cats. Book, books. Dog, dogs. Chair, chairs. Tree, trees.

cards.frontTitle: Rule 2: Ends in s, x, ch, sh → add -es
cards.backTitle: Nouns ending in s, x, ch, sh
cards.explanation: Nouns ending in s, x, ch, sh → add -es so they are easy to say!
cards.speechText: Rule 2: Nouns ending in s, x, c-h, or s-h, add e-s. Bus, buses. Box, boxes. Watch, watches. Brush, brushes. Glass, glasses.

activity.title: Add -s or -es?
activity.instruction: Tap the correct plural for each noun!

items.explanation: Bus ends in s → add -es: buses!
Box ends in x → add -es: boxes!
Watch ends in ch → add -es: watches!

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Subject-Verb Agreement
lessons.description: Make the subject and verb match on the see-saw and play Fix the sentence!
lessons.hint: He, She, It — the -s must fit! I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray!

cards.explanation: Think of a see-saw! The subject and the verb must match in the NOW tense (present).
cards.example: ONE subject 👧 → verb + -s   |   MANY subjects 👧👦 → NO -s
cards.speechText: Make the verb match! Think of a see-saw. The subject and the verb must match in the now tense.

cards.explanation: One person or thing (singular) → verb ends in -s.
cards.speechText: One person or thing, verb ends in s. The student sits. Greta looks for her backpack. Dwayne jumps.

cards.explanation: More than one (plural) → no -s on the verb!
cards.speechText: More than one, no s on the verb. The students sit. My friends run. Stars light up the sky.

cards.frontTitle: Ends in s, sh, ch, tch, z, x → add -es
cards.explanation: Verbs ending in s, sh, ch, tch, z, x → add -es for ONE:
examples: watch → watches  •  teach → teaches  •  reach → reaches
wash → washes  •  mix → mixes  •  fix → fixes
cards.speechText: Verbs ending in s, s-h, c-h, t-c-h, z, or x add e-s for one. Pass, passes. Watch, watches. Mix, mixes. Fix, fixes. Wash, washes. Teach, teaches. Miss, misses. Reach, reaches.

cards.explanation: He, She, or It is ONE → always add -s or -es!
cards.speechText: He, She, or It, add s or e-s. He catches the ball. She picks a movie. It seems late.

cards.explanation: I, You, We, They → NO -s on the verb!
cards.speechText: I, You, We, They, no s. I reach. You tell the truth. We cheer. They walk.

cards.frontHint: A rhyme to help you remember!
cards.explanation: He, She, It — the -s must fit!
cards.example: I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray!
cards.speechText: Memory trick! He, She, It, the s must fit! I, You, We, They, no s, hooray!

activity.title: Fix the sentence!
activity.instruction: Read the wrong sentence, then tap the fixed one!

items.explanation: Harlan is ONE person and fix ends in x → add -es: fixes!

items.wrongSentence: A fly buzz by my ear.
options: A fly buzzes by my ear.
A fly buzzs by my ear.
A fly buzz by my ear.
items.answer: A fly buzzes by my ear.
items.explanation: A fly is ONE thing and buzz ends in z → add -es: buzzes!
I, You, We, They — no -s, hooray! We laugh at the joke.
